mainTopic: Why does our משנה forbid impure hands once the blood has come out? The גמרא tries three explanations: מעשר, first-degree hands, and חולין prepared with the purity of קדשים.
overview: Our משנה forbids eating meat with impure hands once the animal's blood has come out, and the גמרא looks for the case that explains this. First it suggests meat bought with מעשר money, following חכמים, who are stricter than רבי מאיר about מעשר. רב שימי בר אשי objects that חכמים may only forbid eating מעשר, while our משנה is about touching. רב פפא answers instead that the משנה means first-degree hands, following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who holds such hands make even חולין impure. The גמרא shows that first-degree hands really exist, using רבי עקיבא's view about hands put into a בית המנוגע. It then explains why the משנה cannot simply follow רבי עקיבא: his rule may apply only to holy foods, or only to Torah-level impurity. Finally רבי הושעיא explains the משנה as being about חולין prepared with the purity of קדשים, which does not fit רבי יהושע's view. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to suggest yet another way to explain the משנה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Rabbinic impurity affects קדשים and תרומה, not חולין or מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. Something that needs immersion or hand-washing only מדרבנן makes קדשים impure and disqualifies תרומה. According to רבי מאיר, it does nothing to חולין or מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that needs to go into water only because the רבנן said so makes sacred food impure and disqualifies תרומה. It is permitted with ordinary food and with מעשר. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a source to back up its explanation that our משנה is about meat bought with מעשר money. This first part gives רבי מאיר's view, which sets up the disagreement in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things like hands that need washing are only impure מדרבנן, so they have the level of a שני לטומאה. For קדש and תרומה, that level of impurity has an effect. For חולין and, says רבי מאיר, for מעשר too, it has no effect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'going into water': immersion, or washing the hands
By rabbinic law, not from the Torah itself
Disqualifies תרומה: it becomes impure, but cannot pass the impurity on

phrases.english: Anything that requires entry into water
phrases.notes: This covers both a person or object that needs a מקוה and hands that need washing.

phrases.english: by rabbinic law
renders sacred food impure,
and disqualifies terumah,
and is permitted with non-sacred food and with tithe,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַטָּעוּן בִּיאַת מַיִם מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the earlier explanation that our משנה deals with מעשר.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that our משנה is about meat bought with מעשר money, following חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה recording the disagreement between רבי מאיר and חכמים about rabbinic impurity and מעשר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rabbinic-level impurity affects קדש and תרומה, but not חולין or מעשר (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: חכמים forbid it with מעשר
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. They forbid this rabbinic-level impurity with מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים forbid it with מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים say that, unlike חולין, מעשר is affected by this kind of impurity. This is the part the גמרא needs for its explanation of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, מעשר is stricter than ordinary food, so a שני can make it impure. This would explain why our משנה forbids impure hands once the blood made the meat able to become impure, if the meat was bought with מעשר money.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר שני: produce (or food bought with its money) eaten in ירושלים with extra purity rules

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר treats מעשר like חולין. חכמים are stricter with מעשר. But the line does not yet say whether they forbid touching it, eating it, or both.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis prohibit it with tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted source by giving the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that our משנה follows חכמים regarding מעשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of חכמים forbidding rabbinic impurity with מעשר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים forbid rabbinic-level impurity with מעשר.

steps.title: Maybe the Sages only argue about eating tithe
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי asks how we know חכמים forbid touching. Maybe they only argue about eating מעשר, and agree that touching מעשר or eating חולין is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי objects: How do you know? Maybe חכמים argue with רבי מאיר only about eating מעשר. About touching מעשר, or eating חולין, they don't argue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי attacks the proof. The quoted משנה is unclear: it may be about eating only, not touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needs חכמים to forbid impure hands touching מעשר. רב שימי בר אשי suggests a narrower reading: חכמים only forbid a person with a שני-level impurity from eating מעשר. If so, the source cannot explain a case that is about touching.

keyTerms.meaning: He attacked it: a strong objection to a statement
From where? How do you know?

steps.confusionAlert: רב שימי בר אשי is not saying חכמים agree with רבי מאיר completely. He agrees they argue, but suggests they argue only about eating מעשר, not about touching it.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi objects to it:
From where do you know?
phrases.notes: He means: how do you know חכמים forbid touching מעשר?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן
phrases.english: Perhaps the Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi Meir
regarding eating tithe,
but regarding touching tithe
and eating non-sacred food, they do not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: מִמַּאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the quoted source is being read.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that חכמים forbid impure hands touching מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source may only mean eating, so it cannot prove anything about touching.

steps.title: Our משנה is about touching, since someone else might feed him
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says the meat 'is eaten with impure hands.' That covers a case where a friend with impure hands feeds a pure person. So the משנה is about touching, which חכמים may allow with מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this case is about touching, because it says 'they are eaten with impure hands.' Aren't we dealing even with a case where his friend feeds him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי finishes his objection by showing that our משנה is about touching, not eating. So the מעשר explanation doesn't fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the passive wording 'are eaten,' not 'one may eat.' That includes a case where a friend with impure hands feeds a pure person, so the only issue is the friend's hands touching the meat. If חכמים only forbid eating מעשר, touching it would be fine, and the משנה's ruling could not be about מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Aren't we dealing with...? (a way of saying the case surely includes this)

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה is about touching, but חכמים may only argue about eating מעשר. So explaining our משנה as dealing with meat bought with מעשר money now runs into trouble.

phrases.english: But this is a case of touching,
phrases.notes: 'This' means our own משנה about the slaughtered animal, not the משנה just quoted.

phrases.english: since it teaches: 'they are eaten with impure hands,'
are we not dealing
even with a case where his friend feeds him?
phrases.notes: The one eating is pure. Only the friend's impure hands touch the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא נְגִיעָה הִיא, מִדְּקָתָנֵי נֶאֱכָלִין בְּיָדַיִם מְסוֹאָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב שימי בר אשי's objection by showing that our משנה deals with touching.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה is about touching, not eating
steps.raayaSupportSource: The passive wording 'נאכלין בידים מסואבות', which includes a friend feeding a pure person

steps.title: רב פפא: The משנה Means First-Degree Hands
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer. The משנה is talking about hands with first-degree impurity, and it follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: here we are dealing with hands that are first-degree impure, and the משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier approach and gives a fresh answer from רב פפא. The 'impure hands' in our משנה are hands with a stronger, first-degree impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal impure hands are only second-degree, and those cannot make חולין impure anyway. If these hands are first-degree, they can make even חולין impure. That explains why the משנה forbids impure hands once the blood has come out and made the meat able to become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather — the גמרא is dropping the previous answer and offering a new one

steps.confusionAlert: Usually impure hands are only שניות (second-degree). רב פפא is saying this משנה is about an unusual case where hands are תחלות (first-degree).

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Here we are dealing with hands that are first-degree impure,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our משנה, which said the meat may be eaten with impure hands.

phrases.english: and it follows the view of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier explanation with a new reading of the משנה's 'impure hands'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (which kind of impure hands) and naming whose opinion the משנה follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'impure hands' are ordinary second-degree hands, and the point is about touching מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means first-degree hands, which can make even חולין impure, following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא: Can Hands Make חולין Impure?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows an argument. The first opinion says hands do not count as first-degree for חולין. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי מאיר says they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: hands are not first-degree for חולין. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: hands are first-degree for חולין, and second-degree for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's opinion, which רב פפא is relying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion holds that hands never make חולין impure, even when they are first-degree. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says first-degree hands do make חולין impure. That is exactly what רב פפא needs to explain the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Second-degree impurity; such hands only disqualify תרומה

phrases.english: As it is taught: Hands are not first-degree for non-holy food;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Hands that are first-degree count for non-holy food,
and second-degree hands count for תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין יָדַיִם תְּחִלּוֹת לַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the opinion רב פפא just named.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a view under which first-degree hands make חולין impure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי מאיר

steps.title: Only חולין and Not תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the wording. Does it mean first-degree hands affect חולין but not תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: First-degree for חולין, yes, but for תרומה, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Read simply, it sounds like first-degree hands affect only חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה is holier than חולין. It makes no sense that hands could make חולין impure but not תרומה. So the plain reading cannot be right.

phrases.english: First-degree for non-holy food, yes,
but for תרומה, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּחִלּוֹת לְחוּלִּין – אִין, לִתְרוּמָה – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the ברייתא just quoted is worded.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read simply, it suggests first-degree hands do not affect תרומה, which is holier. That is illogical.

steps.title: What רבי שמעון בן אלעזר Really Means
steps.stepSummary: First-degree hands make even חולין impure, and of course תרומה too. Second-degree hands affect תרומה but not חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: first-degree hands affect even חולין. Second-degree hands affect תרומה, yes, but חולין, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the correct way to read רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' is the key. First-degree hands are strong enough to make even חולין impure, so surely they affect תרומה. The weaker second-degree hands only affect תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means — rereading a statement

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, first-degree hands make even חולין impure. Second-degree hands only affect תרומה.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
First-degree hands affect even non-holy food;
second-degree hands affect תרומה, yes,
but non-holy food, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge by rereading the statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: First-degree hands affect only חולין and not תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: First-degree hands affect even חולין (and of course תרומה). Second-degree hands affect only תרומה.

steps.title: Can Hands Ever Be First-Degree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether there is any real case where hands become first-degree impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there really such a thing as first-degree hands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רב פפא's case can even exist. This sets up the next step, which brings a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hands are usually treated as second-degree. If hands can never be first-degree, רב פפא's explanation would not work.

phrases.english: And is there such a thing as first-degree hands?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא יָדַיִם תְּחִלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the case רב פפא described can ever happen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hands can ever have first-degree impurity

steps.title: Hands Inside a House with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: Yes. רבי עקיבא says that if someone puts his hands into a בית המנוגע, his hands become first-degree. חכמים say second-degree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as it is taught: if someone put his hands into a house with צרעת, his hands are first-degree, according to רבי עקיבא. חכמים say his hands are second-degree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes and brings a source: hands put into a house with צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, hands can be first-degree impure. So there is a real case of ידים תחלות, and רב פפא's explanation can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A house struck with צרעת, which makes people who enter it impure

phrases.english: Yes, as it is taught:
If someone put his hands into a house with צרעת,
his hands are first-degree; these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say: his hands are second-degree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּתַנְיָא: הִכְנִיס יָדָיו לְבַיִת הַמְנוּגָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing a case of first-degree hands.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. According to רבי עקיבא, hands put into a בית המנוגע become first-degree.

steps.title: The Dispute Is Only About a Rabbinic Decree
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that partly entering a house does not count as entering. They argue only about a rabbinic decree that treats the hands as impure because of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that entering partway is not called entering. Here they argue about a decree on the hands because of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי עקיבא and חכמים are really arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, putting only your hands into the house does not make you impure, since partial entry is not 'entry'. The Rabbis made a decree that the hands are impure, because people might come to enter with the whole body. רבי עקיבא and חכמים argue only about how strong that decree is: first-degree or second-degree.

keyTerms.meaning: Partial entry (only part of the body goes in)
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Because of / on account of (something else)

steps.whatToRemember: Hands put into a בית המנוגע are impure only by rabbinic decree, because people might come to enter with the whole body. רבי עקיבא makes that decree first-degree, so first-degree hands do exist.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא holds that partial entry counts as entry by Torah law. Everyone agrees it does not. The argument is only about a decree.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees
that partial entry is not called entry,
and here, it is about a decree
on his hands because of his body that they disagree.
phrases.notes: He means: the Rabbis made the hands impure so people won't come to put their whole body into the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בִּיאָה בְּמִקְצָת לֹא שְׁמָהּ בִּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis of the argument in the source just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partial entry is not entry by Torah law. The hands' impurity is a rabbinic decree, and the argument is about how strong that decree is.

steps.title: The two views on how the decree treats the hands
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds the רבנן treated the hands like the body, so they are first-degree. The חכמים hold the רבנן treated them like ordinary hands, so they are second-degree.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds the רבנן made his hands like his body. The other Sage holds the רבנן made the hands like ordinary hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation from Step 11. It shows exactly what each side thinks the rabbinic decree said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the hands are impure only because of a rabbinic decree. רבי עקיבא says the decree treats the hands as if the whole body went in, so they become a תחילה. The חכמים say the decree gave them the usual status of hands, which is שניות.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן made them (gave them this status)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת is about which model the decree used: 'like the body' (first-degree) or 'like regular hands' (second-degree).

phrases.english: One Sage holds: his hands are like his body
phrases.notes: This 'one Sage' is רבי עקיבא, who said the hands become first-degree.

phrases.english: the Rabbis made them;
and the other Sage holds: hands
the Rabbis made them like ordinary hands.
phrases.notes: Ordinary hands are treated by the רבנן as second-degree.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: יָדָיו – כְּגוּפוֹ שַׁוִּינְהוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes Step 11 by spelling out the reasoning of each side about the rabbinic decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: hands are like the body, so first-degree. חכמים: hands are like ordinary hands, so second-degree.

steps.title: Why not explain the משנה like רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the earlier explanation of the משנה did not simply follow רבי עקיבא, who holds that hands can become first-degree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him explain it like רבי עקיבא, who says his hands become first-degree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier explanation of the משנה. רבי עקיבא already gives us a case of first-degree hands, so why not use him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of hands that are first-degree. Step 10 just showed that רבי עקיבא holds exactly that in the בית המנוגע case. So it seems easier to say the משנה follows רבי עקיבא than to look for a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him establish it (explain the משנה as following)

phrases.english: But let him establish it according to Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה about first-degree hands. The question is why the earlier explanation picked a different תנא.

phrases.english: who says: his hands become first-degree?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא's view from Steps 10-12 to question how the משנה was explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation of the משנה, which did not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא gives a ready case of first-degree hands, so the משנה should be explained like him.

steps.title: Maybe רבי עקיבא meant only תרומה and קדשים
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps רבי עקיבא said the hands are first-degree only for the stricter foods, תרומה and קדשים. For חולין they would be only second-degree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps when רבי עקיבא said this, it was only for תרומה and קדשים, which are strict. But for חולין, the hands are second-degree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי עקיבא's 'first-degree' may only apply to holy foods, so he does not fit a משנה about first-degree hands for חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא needs hands that make even חולין impure (step 5). If רבי עקיבא's hands are first-degree only for תרומה and קדשים, then for חולין they are just שניות. So his view would not fit the משנה.

phrases.english: Perhaps when Rabbi Akiva says it,
that applies only to terumah and sacrificial food,
which are stringent,
but for non-sacred food, they are second-degree.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּתְרוּמָה וְקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by limiting רבי עקיבא's ruling to holy foods.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the opinion (only stricter foods)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's first-degree hands apply everywhere, so the משנה fits him.
steps.terutzMaskana: His first-degree status may apply only to תרומה and קדשים. For חולין the hands are second-degree, so he does not fit the משנה.

steps.title: Even second-degree hands affect חולין for רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even if the hands are only second-degree for חולין, רבי עקיבא holds that a שני makes a שלישי in חולין. So the hands would still affect חולין, and the משנה could still follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them also be second-degree. We have heard that רבי עקיבא says a שני makes a שלישי in חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 14. Being second-degree does not stop the hands from making חולין impure according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a שני cannot make חולין impure. But רבי עקיבא holds that a שני does create a שלישי even in חולין. So the hands would still affect חולין in his view, and the reason for not using him seems to fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: A second-degree item makes a third-degree item in חולין

steps.confusionAlert: Usually חולין cannot go past a שני, so a שלישי in חולין is just pure. רבי עקיבא's view is the special exception here, not the normal rule.

phrases.english: And let them also be second-degree,
phrases.notes: He means: fine, say the hands are second-degree for חולין. The משנה could still follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: for we have heard that Rabbi Akiva
says: a second-degree item makes a third-degree item in non-sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיהֶוְיָין נָמֵי שְׁנִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14 using another known ruling of רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 14, which says רבי עקיבא's hands are only second-degree for חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי עקיבא even a שני affects חולין, so second-degree hands would still make חולין impure. The משנה could still follow him.

steps.title: The source: רבי עקיבא's דרשה on 'יטמא'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבי עקיבא's view from a משנה. He reads the פסוק's word 'יטמא' to mean the item makes others impure. This teaches that a second-degree loaf makes a third-degree in חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: On that day רבי עקיבא taught: 'And every earthenware vessel... shall be impure.' It does not say 'is impure' but 'יטמא': to make others impure. This teaches about a second-degree loaf, that it makes a שלישי in חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim in Step 15. It shows that רבי עקיבא really holds a שני makes a שלישי in חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food inside the כלי חרס is already a שני. The פסוק could have said 'טמא' (is impure) but says 'יטמא'. רבי עקיבא learns from this extra wording that this loaf passes impurity on, creating a שלישי even in חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: On that day (a well-known day of many teachings)
Shall be impure; read here as able to make others impure

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns from 'יטמא' that a שני makes a שלישי in חולין. This is why second-degree hands would still matter for חולין in his view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה is the famous source for רבי עקיבא's view that impurity can reach a שלישי in חולין. That view is what keeps the option of explaining the משנה like him alive.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן, בּוֹ בְּיוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: As we learned: On that day Rabbi Akiva expounded:
"And every earthenware vessel, etc., shall be impure,"
it does not say "is impure,"
but rather "shall be impure": to make others impure,
this teaches about a second-degree loaf
that it makes a third-degree item in non-sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, בּוֹ בְּיוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבי עקיבא's ruling quoted in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי עקיבא holds a שני makes a שלישי in חולין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of 'בו ביום', where רבי עקיבא expounds 'יטמא' in ויקרא 11:33

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's rule may only apply to Torah-level impurity
steps.stepSummary: The proof from רבי עקיבא is pushed away. Maybe a שני makes a שלישי in חולין only when the impurity is from the Torah, not when it is rabbinic, like hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this rule applies only to impurity from the Torah, but not to impurity from the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea from steps 15–16 that the משנה could follow רבי עקיבא. His rule may cover only Torah-level impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, רבי עקיבא learned from the word 'יטמא' that a שני makes a שלישי in חולין. That was about a real Torah impurity, like a שרץ. The impurity of hands is only rabbinic, so his rule may not apply to it, and the משנה still cannot be explained as following him.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; maybe (used to push back on a proof)
These words apply (this rule is limited to)
Impurity that comes from the Torah itself
From the רבנן; a rabbinic rule

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי עקיבא's rule is wrong. It is only limiting it to Torah impurity, so it may not cover hands, which are impure only by rabbinic law.

phrases.english: Perhaps these words apply
phrases.notes: He means רבי עקיבא's rule from step 16, that a שני makes a שלישי in חולין.

phrases.english: only to impurity by Torah law,
but to rabbinic impurity, not.
phrases.notes: The impurity of hands is only rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּטוּמְאָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 16 by limiting רבי עקיבא's rule to Torah-level impurity.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה can follow רבי עקיבא, because his rule may not reach rabbinic impurity of hands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof was about a Torah impurity, so it cannot be stretched to a rabbinic impurity like hands.

steps.title: A new explanation: non-sacred food handled with the purity of sacred food
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי הושעיא, explains that the משנה is about חולין that were prepared with the purity of קדשים, and that it does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי הושעיא: Here we are dealing with חולין that were prepared with the purity of קדשים, and the משנה does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to explain the משנה. It is about חולין that someone chose to handle as carefully as קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanations got stuck on whether hands can affect plain חולין. רבי הושעיא solves this by saying these חולין were treated like קדשים, so they can be affected at a deeper level. He adds that this explanation does not follow רבי יהושע, and the next steps bring the source for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-sacred food that was prepared with the strict purity rules of קדשים

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the third approach to the משנה, and it changes the case itself instead of looking for a תנא who holds that hands affect plain חולין.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Hoshaya said:
Here, with non-sacred food
that was prepared with the purity of sacred food, we are dealing,
and it is not following Rabbi Yehoshua,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא הָכָא בְּחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבי עקיבא approach was rejected, this offers a fresh explanation of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה deals with חולין prepared with the purity of קדשים, and it does not follow רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: you become the same degree as the food you ate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source. רבי אליעזר says a person who eats impure food takes on the same level of impurity as that food: first, second, or third.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי אליעזר says: One who eats first-degree food becomes first-degree. One who eats second-degree food becomes second-degree. One who eats third-degree food becomes third-degree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind 'not following רבי יהושע'. First it gives רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the person simply takes on the exact level of the food he ate. So eating third-degree food makes him only third-degree. This shows he treats a third-degree level as real for this kind of food.

keyTerms.meaning: One who eats food (that is impure)

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר, not the רבי אלעזר from the step before. The names look alike.

phrases.english: One who eats first-degree food becomes first-degree,
second-degree food, second-degree,
third-degree food, third-degree.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר הָאוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא behind רבי הושעיא's words 'not following רבי יהושע'.
steps.raayaObject: רבי הושעיא's explanation and its link to the מחלוקת in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about one who eats impure food.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: eating makes you second-degree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע disagrees. Eating first- or second-degree food makes a person second-degree. Eating third-degree food makes him second-degree only for קדשים, not for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: One who eats first-degree or second-degree food becomes second-degree. One who eats third-degree food becomes second-degree for קדשים, but not second-degree for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי יהושע's opposing view. This is the opinion the משנה does not follow, according to רבי הושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע does not match the person to the food's level. Anyone who eats first- or second-degree food becomes second-degree. Eating third-degree food counts as second-degree only toward the holiest food, קדשים, and not toward תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Counts as second-degree when it comes to קדשים
But does not count as second-degree when it comes to תרומה
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
One who eats first-degree or second-degree food becomes second-degree,
third-degree food, second-degree for sacred food,
but not second-degree for תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר הָאוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the ברייתא's מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: Shows the view of רבי יהושע, which רבי הושעיא says the משנה does not follow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the same ברייתא.

steps.title: Third-degree food that someone eats is non-sacred food handled like תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the case of eating third-degree food must be about חולין handled with the purity of תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is about חולין that were prepared with the purity of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears up the ברייתא's case of eating third-degree food. It explains what kind of food that must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain חולין cannot become third-degree, and impure תרומה or קדשים may not be eaten. So the only way to eat third-degree food is if it is חולין that someone handled with the purity of תרומה. This fits רבי הושעיא's idea that חולין handled at a higher purity level can be affected at a deeper level.

keyTerms.meaning: The purity level required for תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי הושעיא explains the משנה as talking about חולין handled with extra purity. The ברייתא shows that such חולין can reach a third-degree level. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about what happens to the person who eats impure food.

phrases.english: With non-sacred food that was prepared with the purity of תרומה.
phrases.notes: This explains the 'third-degree food' in the ברייתא. Plain חולין can't be third-degree, so it must be food handled like תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case in the ברייתא just quoted, where someone eats third-degree food.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might ask how anyone could eat third-degree food at all, since plain חולין cannot become third-degree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is חולין handled with the purity of תרומה, which can reach third-degree and may still be eaten.

steps.title: רבי יהושע holds that חולין kept with the purity of קדשים have no שלישי
steps.stepSummary: The case of eating third-degree food works only for חולין handled with the purity of תרומה, not with the purity of קדשים. So רבי יהושע must hold that חולין handled with the purity of קדשים cannot become a שלישי.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the purity of תרומה, yes. With the purity of קדשים, no. This shows he holds that ordinary food prepared with the purity of קדשים has no third degree of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the answer in step 21. It explains exactly what רבי יהושע must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source in step 21 specifies that רבי יהושע's third-degree food is חולין handled with the purity of תרומה. Why didn't it say the purity of קדשים? Because רבי יהושע holds that such חולין cannot become a שלישי at all. This is why רבי הושעיא (step 18) said the משנה, which is about חולין prepared with the purity of קדשים, does not follow רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: The higher purity level used for sacred food (קדשים).
He holds. This brings in the opinion that a sage must hold, based on what he said.
There is not in them; they do not have

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע, חולין handled with the purity of תרומה can become a שלישי. חולין handled with the purity of קדשים cannot. So the משנה, which gives such חולין a שלישי, does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not get mixed up here. The higher purity (קדשים) is the one that does NOT give חולין a שלישי according to רבי יהושע. Being more careful does not make ordinary food act like קדשים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the proof for רבי הושעיא's claim in step 18 that the משנה does not follow רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: With the purity of teruma, yes.
phrases.notes: This means חולין handled as carefully as תרומה. Those can become a third degree, as in רבי יהושע's case.

phrases.english: With the purity of sacred food, no.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: חוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ
phrases.english: He holds: non-sacred food prepared with the purity of sacred food
has no third degree in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל טׇהֳרַת תְּרוּמָה – אִין, עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ – לָא, קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the logical result of step 21's answer and shows what רבי יהושע holds.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע holds that חולין prepared with the purity of קדשים have no שלישי. So the משנה does not follow him, just as רבי הושעיא said.

steps.title: Opening a challenge: why not explain the משנה differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge. It suggests explaining the משנה in a different way. The full suggestion continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us explain the משנה as being about...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts to ask why we don't explain the משנה in another way, and the rest of the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, רבי הושעיא explained the משנה as being about חולין prepared with the purity of קדשים, which goes against רבי יהושע. The word וְלוֹקְמַהּ opens a push back. Maybe the משנה could be explained in a way that fits רבי יהושע too. The details come in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us establish it. This means: why not explain the source as talking about a different case?

phrases.english: But let us establish it
phrases.notes: "It" means the משנה. The גמרא is about to suggest a different case for it, and the rest comes in the next lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי הושעיא's explanation of the משנה (step 18), now that step 22 showed it goes against רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי הושעיא's claim that the משנה is about חולין prepared with the purity of קדשים and does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is better to explain a משנה so that it fits more opinions. The גמרא is about to suggest another case that would keep the משנה in line with רבי יהושע.
